text:
sam: kicking off evaluation for alder-embed-lite (256d) w/ post-training static int4 (per-channel) and a dynamic 6-bit run for comparison. goal: measure short-tail recall and MRR on our labeled holdouts + semantic clusters.

lina: nice. which holdouts exactly? and are you running precision@k or MRR?

sam: using holdouts: prod-qa-20k (mixed-length), shorttail-5k (queries <= 16 tokens), and cluster-probes-10k (labelled clusters). metrics: recall@1,5,10, mrr@10, precision@5, and nn-islanding (fraction of queries whose top10 are all same class). harness command below:

```
./eval/run_shim \\
  --model alder-embed-lite \\
  --quant static-int4,dynamic6 \\
  --datasets prod-qa-20k,shorttail-5k,cluster-probes-10k \\
  --metrics recall@1,5,10,mrr@10,precision@5,nn-islanding,cosine-drift \\
  --batch 512 --seed 7 \\
  --save artifacts/alder/3755554321 \\
  --threads 16
```

mohit: curious about cosine-drift. that's the per-query change in cos(sim(true_nn), sim(model_nn))?

sam: yup, and also a per-query nearest-neighbor swap count (how many of top10 changed). first-pass quick numbers (static-int4 vs baseline bert-embed-base):
- prod-qa recall@5: baseline 0.682 -> alder-static-int4 0.651 (delta -0.031)
- shorttail recall@1: baseline 0.512 -> alder-static-int4 0.453 (delta -0.059)
- mrr@10 (shorttail): baseline 0.428 -> alder-static-int4 0.366
- precision@5 (clusters): 0.74 -> 0.70
- nn-islanding (clusters): baseline 0.12 -> alder 0.18 (higher islanding)
- mean top10 swap count: 2.3 changed vs baseline
- cosine-drift median: -0.019 (model lowers similarity to true-nn)
- perf: latency static-int4 3.6ms/vec, dynamic6 5.0ms/vec, baseline 9.2ms/vec

eval-bot: artifacts uploaded: https://internal.redwood/artefacts/alder/3755554321 (contains per-query waterfall, cos-drift heatmap, nn-swap distributions). significance tests: shorttail recall@1 drop p < 0.001.

lina: those shorttail numbers are concerning. does the failure concentrate on named-entity queries or very short paraphrases? can you run a confusion matrix over the labelled shorttail set (NE vs faq vs title)?

sam: running that now. initial glance at per-class deltas: NE (named-entity) recall@1 down 12 pts, faq down 4 pts, titles down 6 pts. NE examples look like: tokens are very short (2-3 tokens) and nearest neighbour shifts to same-class but wrong entity.

mohit: my hypothesis: quantized embedding table causes small angular shifts that are enough to cross decision boundary for short queries where margin is small. try: 1) L2-normalize embeddings post-quant, 2) calibrate embedding table with more calibration vectors emphasizing short queries, 3) try asymmetric quant (scale+zero) per-row.

sam: will run L2-normalize and a calibration set augmented with shorttail examples. also trying an ensemble fallback: if qlen<=8 then route to bert-embed-base; else use alder. need quick cost estimate for that routing.

ops-bot: estimated cost impact for routing shorttail->bert-embed-base: +2.1% token cost at current traffic mix (shorttail ~6% of queries). latency P95 for mixed route increases by +30ms for the routed portion.

lina: maybe instead of full routing we can run a light-weight reranker: use alder to fetch top50 then rerank with bert-embed for qlen<=8 only. lower cost than full routing.

sam: good tradeoff. I'll prototype top50 fetch + rerank (bert-embed scorer) and compare recall vs full-route. also running per-channel-int4 static vs per-channel int3 (experimental) to see sensitivity.

mohit: if reranker recovers >90% of the shorttail loss at <10% extra cost, shipable as a temporary mitigation. otherwise we need to revisit quant scheme.

sam: noted. I'll post follow-ups and the confusion matrix in ~45m. thanks all. :rocket:
